root_causes.root_cause: Docling TableFormer cannot extract vector-icon table cells (checkmarks/symbols rendered as PDF path operators, not text glyphs). The Unfallversicherung benefit-comparison table has 75% empty cells because cell content is rasterized vector icons invisible to text-layer extraction. flat_char_count (7,408) includes table row_records pipe-delimited structure, while non-table block text is only 492 chars. RFC-027 D0 fixed the enrichment-metadata inflation (old _flat_block_text -> new _flat_block_primary_text), but the underlying TableFormer cell extraction failure persists.
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:pdf_to_markdown_docling -> Docling TableFormer ACCURATE mode -> helpers.py:_flat_parse_table -> helpers.py:flag_empty_cells
root_causes.suggested_fix: Cell-level rasterization+OCR for table cells with zero text content but non-zero visual content (vector-icon path operators). RFC-027 explicitly deferred this as follow-up RFC-028 candidate. Alternative: Docling upstream enhancement for path-operator glyph recognition.

root_causes.root_cause: Scanned Arabic PDF OCR recovery is partial: RFC-027 D2 low-content OCR escalation improved this doc from ~60 chars to 5,972 chars (75 blocks), but char density (~1493/page) is still 50-60% of expected norm (2000-4000/page). Two compounding factors: (a) Tesseract Arabic OCR on scanned pages produces incomplete output (missed lines/words), (b) flat structure (depth=0) persists because OCR output lacks the Arabic structural markers (_AR_PART_RE/_AR_ARTICLE_RE) that _inject_arabic_structural_headings needs to create headings.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Investigate Tesseract OCR quality on this specific scanned Arabic PDF: (1) check DPI of the scanned pages vs the 300 DPI crop setting, (2) verify ara.traineddata quality (best vs fast model), (3) consider pre-processing (binarization/deskew) before OCR. For depth: Arabic structural heading injection threshold (len(t) <= 60) may need tuning for scanned OCR output where structural markers are partially recovered.
